stages.name: Sicels, Elymians, Italics
stages.desc: Native peoples: Sicel and Elymian towns, Lucanians, Samnites, Messapians, Sardinians

stages.name: Independent Greek
stages.desc: Self-governing Greek cities outside Dionysius' rule

stages.name: Syracusan allies
stages.desc: Cities and peoples bound to Dionysius by alliance or treaty

stages.name: Syracusan-ruled
stages.desc: Held directly by Dionysius and his garrisons

stages.name: Contested
stages.desc: Fought over, or split by the war's frontier

timeline: Samnite highlands

states.name: Foggia
timeline: The Daunian plains of northern Apulia

states.name: Barletta-Andria-Trani
timeline: Daunian and Peucetian country

states.name: Bari
timeline: Peucetian towns of the Apulian coast

states.name: Brindisi
timeline: Messapian towns around the harbour of Brundisium

states.name: Lecce
timeline: Messapian towns of the Salento

states.name: Taranto
timeline: Taras, the strongest Greek city in Italy, later led by the philosopher Archytas

states.name: Matera
timeline: Metapontum and Heraclea on the Gulf of Taranto

states.name: Cosenza
timeline: Lucanians and Bruttians in the hills; Greek Thurii on the coast
The Lucanians crush the army of Thurii near Laus

states.name: Crotone
timeline: Croton, the leading city of the Italiote League
Dionysius seizes Croton (date approximate) and holds it for about twelve years

states.name: Catanzaro
timeline: Scylletium and the Greek lands of the narrow isthmus
Dionysius holds the isthmus and plans a wall across it against the Lucanians

states.name: Reggio Calabria
timeline: Rhegium, Dionysius' bitterest Greek enemy; Locri, to the east, is his ally
Dionysius razes Caulonia and forces Rhegium to pay three hundred talents
Siege of Rhegium
Rhegium falls after eleven months; its people are sold into slavery

states.name: Vibo Valentia
timeline: Hipponium, a Greek city allied with Dionysius' enemies
Dionysius razes Hipponium and gives its land to his ally Locri
Carthage restores the exiled Hipponiates to their city

states.name: Potenza
timeline: Lucanian hill country
The Lucanians ally with Dionysius against the Italian Greeks

states.name: Salerno
timeline: Poseidonia, now ruled by Lucanians; Greek Elea holds out on the coast

states.name: Naples
timeline: Neapolis, a Greek city among the Campanians

states.name: Caserta
timeline: Capua and the Oscan-speaking Campanians, prized as mercenaries by Dionysius

states.name: Latina
timeline: Volscian and Latin country south of Rome

states.name: Trapani
timeline: Lilybaeum, Carthage's stronghold after Motya; Selinus and the Elymian cities under Carthage
Cities subject to Carthage go over to Dionysius; war resumes (dates disputed, 383–c. 375)
Peace: Carthage keeps the west, with Selinus and its territory
Dionysius takes Selinus, Entella and Eryx and besieges Lilybaeum
After the winter truce and Dionysius' death, the west returns to Carthage

states.name: Messina
timeline: Mago fights from the Sicel town of Abacaenum; Sicels hold Tauromenium
Dionysius takes Tauromenium and settles his mercenaries; Messana and Tyndaris are his

states.name: Palermo
timeline: Panormus, Solus and Thermae: the heart of Carthage's Sicilian province
Battle of Cronium near Panormus: Leptines is killed (date disputed, 383–c. 375)

states.name: Agrigento
timeline: Acragas, sacked by Carthage in 406, rebuilt and self-governing
War: the land between Acragas and Selinus becomes a battleground (dates disputed, 383–c. 375)
Peace: Carthage takes Acragantine land west of the Halycus river, the new frontier

states.name: Caltanissetta
timeline: Gela, freed from tribute to Carthage in 397, follows Dionysius

states.name: Ragusa
timeline: Camarina, freed from tribute to Carthage in 397, follows Dionysius

states.name: Syracuse
timeline: Syracuse, Dionysius' capital, ruled from the walled island citadel of Ortygia
Deportees from Caulonia and Hipponium are settled in Syracuse
Dionysius dies; his son Dionysius II inherits the tyranny

states.name: Catania
timeline: Catana and Leontini, emptied of their citizens and held by Dionysius' mercenaries

states.name: Carbonia-Iglesias
timeline: Sulcis and the Carthaginian mining country of the south-west

states.name: Sassari
timeline: Nuragic Sardinians of the north-west

states.name: Nuoro
timeline: Nuragic Sardinians of the mountains, outside Carthage's control

states.name: Olbia-Tempio
timeline: Nuragic Sardinians of Gallura

states.name: Oristano
timeline: Tharros, a Phoenician harbour city under Carthage

states.name: Medio Campidano
timeline: The Campidano plain, Carthage's grain land in Sardinia

states.name: Cagliari
timeline: Karalis and the Carthaginian south of Sardinia
Sardinians rise against Carthage, together with the Libyans in Africa

states.name: Ogliastra
timeline: Nuragic Sardinians of the eastern mountains

states.name: Enna

events.title: Mago beaten
events.text: In 393/392 BC the Carthaginian general Mago is defeated near the Sicel town of Abacaenum, losing some eight hundred men.

events.title: Night attack on Rhegium
events.text: Dionysius tries to take Rhegium by surprise at night and fails.

events.title: Standoff on the Chrysas
events.text: Mago's eighty thousand face Dionysius and Agyris of Agyrium; neither side risks a battle.

events.title: Peace of 392
events.text: Carthage keeps the west; the Sicels are left subject to Dionysius, who is granted Tauromenium.

events.title: Tauromenium taken
events.text: Dionysius expels most of the Sicels and settles his best mercenaries in their hill town.

events.title: Lucanian alliance
events.text: Dionysius allies with the Lucanians, the Italic people pressing on the Greek cities.

events.title: Italiote League
events.text: The Greek cities of southern Italy unite against Dionysius and the Lucanians.

events.title: Storm off Rhegium
events.text: A storm wrecks part of Dionysius' fleet as he attacks Rhegium.

events.title: Disaster at Laus
events.text: The Lucanians destroy the army of Thurii; Leptines shelters the survivors and is dismissed for it.

events.title: Battle of the Elleporus
events.text: Dionysius routs the Italiote League, kills its general Heloris and frees ten thousand prisoners without ransom.

events.title: Caulonia razed
events.text: The city is destroyed, its people moved to Syracuse and its land given to Locri.

events.title: Rhegium pays
events.text: Rhegium buys a truce with three hundred talents, seventy ships and a hundred hostages.

events.title: Hipponium razed
events.text: Its people are deported to Syracuse and its land given to Locri.

events.title: Locri rewarded
events.text: Locri, home of Dionysius' wife Doris, becomes his chief ally in Italy.

events.title: Plato in Taras
events.text: Plato visits Archytas of Taras before sailing on to Sicily.

events.title: Siege of Rhegium
events.text: Dionysius blockades the city by land and sea.

events.title: Rhegium falls
events.text: After eleven months the starving city surrenders; its general Phyton is tortured and drowned.

events.title: Plato at Syracuse
events.text: Plato visits the court; tradition says he was sold as a slave and ransomed by friends.

events.title: Into the Adriatic
events.text: Dionysius' fleets command the passage to the Adriatic, where he founds Lissus and helps settle Pharos.

events.title: Cities defect
events.text: Dionysius stirs Carthage's subject cities to revolt; Diodorus dates the new war to 383 BC.

events.title: Battle of Cabala
events.text: Mago is killed with over ten thousand men; site unknown, date between 383 and c. 375 BC.

events.title: Plague in Carthage
events.text: Plague and a Libyan revolt bring Carthage near to ruin.

events.title: Sardinia rises
events.text: The Sardinians revolt against Carthage.

events.title: Hipponium restored
events.text: Carthage brings the exiles of Hipponium home.

events.title: Croton seized
events.text: Dionysius takes Croton, the Italiote League's leading city (date approximate).

events.title: A wall across Italy
events.text: Dionysius plans a wall across the isthmus of Scylletium against the Lucanians.

events.title: Battle of Cronium
events.text: Near Panormus, Mago's son defeats Dionysius; Leptines and fourteen thousand Greeks fall (date disputed).

events.title: Peace on the Halycus
events.text: Dionysius pays a thousand talents and cedes Selinus and the land west of the Halycus.

events.title: Ships lost at Corcyra
events.text: Nine of ten Syracusan triremes sent to aid Sparta are captured by the Athenian Iphicrates.

events.title: Mercenaries for Sparta
events.text: Dionysius sends two thousand Celts and Iberians to fight for Sparta in Greece.

events.title: Athens honours him
events.text: Athens grants Dionysius and his sons citizenship.

events.title: Selinus taken
events.text: Dionysius invades with thirty thousand foot, three thousand horse and three hundred warships.

events.title: Entella and Eryx
events.text: The Elymian towns of Entella and Eryx go over to Dionysius.

events.title: Siege of Lilybaeum
events.text: Carthage's fortress holds; Dionysius abandons the siege.

events.title: Fleet lost at Eryx
events.text: Two hundred Carthaginian warships surprise his fleet in the harbour and capture most of it.

events.title: Alliance with Athens
events.text: Athens and Dionysius conclude a defensive alliance.

events.title: The Ransom of Hector
events.text: Dionysius' tragedy wins first prize at the Lenaia festival in Athens.

events.title: Death of Dionysius
events.text: He dies after a victory feast, aged about sixty-five, after thirty-eight years in power.

events.title: Dionysius II
events.text: His son inherits the tyranny and soon makes peace with Carthage.

chartNote: Share of the area of today's provinces of Sicily, Sardinia and southern Italy, by who controlled most of each. Ancient territories followed cities and rivers, not modern borders, so this is a simplification. The dates of Cabala and Cronium are disputed (383–c. 375 BC); the war is shown as contested over that whole range.
